subject: hedgehog
pitch: A plump hedgehog out on an autumn evening walk. A dome of spines in chestnut brown with cream tips, a soft fawn face with a pointed, twitchy snout, a shiny black button nose, tiny round ears and bright beady eyes. Little pink paws, and a single red maple leaf stuck on its spines like a trophy.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a hedgehog model using the SDK, scaling it realistically at about 25cm long, and thinking through building the plump body as an ellipsoid shape with scattered spikes projecting outward from a dome-shaped region on its back.

For the spines, I'm figuring out how to give each spike a brown base with a cream tip by using a color function or paint based on the sweep parameter along the spike's length, since the spike's t-value runs from base (0) to tip (1).

Now I'm shifting to designing the body: a dome-shaped hedgehog form built with lofted stations along a spine chain from hips to neck, defining width and height at each z-position and attaching joints for the body's curvature and posture.

For the head, I'm planning a tapered sweep from the head joint down to the snout tip, so the face comes to a point naturally.

For coloring, I'm giving the face a fawn tone and keeping spine spikes limited to the back and upper body, filtering out the front and head regions when I scatter them.

Each spike is built as its own small sweep part oriented along the surface normal, tapering to a point with a small base radius, and with around 300-320 of them scattered using a seeded RNG and minimum distance spacing, the triangle budget stays well within limits. I'm filtering the scatter points by position and normal direction so spikes only appear on the back, not the belly or face.

For the face, I'm planning the eyes as small black sphere parts placed via local coordinates on the head (using forward/up/left offsets), possibly with a white highlight dot for a beady look, and considering whether the head sweep's radius at that point will actually support surface placement cleanly.

I'm figuring out the nose as a tiny black button placed at the snout tip using the surface nearest-point method, and working out how to add small rounded ears by scaling flattened sphere geometry and sticking them onto the head surface near the top sides.

For legs, I'm building short two-segment limb chains for each paw with named joints (hip, knee, ankle) so each chain produces the right number of bend points, then capping each foot with a small flattened pink sphere to look like a paw pad.

I'm placing hip roots near the lower body — front legs forward near the shoulders, back legs near the haunches — with chains parented to the hips joint so they inherit body movement correctly.

For the leaf, I want it stuck flat atop the spines on the back, so I'm finding the nearest surface point there and orienting the leaf's extrusion plane so its thickness runs along world Y, making it lie horizontally. Now I'm sketching a palmate maple-leaf outline with several pointed lobes to extrude from.

Still mapping out leaf outline points...

For placement, I'm thinking the leaf should rest near the top of the body, slightly above the spine tips, using a nearest-point lookup and an offset along the normal so it looks stuck on rather than floating. I'll keep colors simple — a reddish tone for the leaf and a brownish tone for the body — rather than adding extra vein details or stray spikes.

Now I'm working out the body shape using a loft across several stations with varying width and height so the hedgehog looks properly plump, choosing a brown body tone with cream spine tips and a fawn face. I need to adjust the vertical placement of these stations so the body sits convincingly above the legs rather than sinking to the ground or floating too high, settling on a center height around 0.13 with hip joints positioned on the sides where the legs attach.

For the head, I'm sweeping a tapered path from a wider base near the body to a pointed snout tip, shrinking the radius as it goes forward so it overlaps naturally into the body's front face. Then I'm setting up the ears to sit near the top of the head tube and working out how to define the head as a short joint chain so I can attach features to it properly.

For eye placement I'm computing where on the head's surface a given point lands by checking its distance from the tube's central axis against the local radius at that cross-section, so eyes projected slightly inside the tube still snap outward to the correct surface position.

For the highlight, I'm adding a tiny white sphere offset along the surface normal from the eye hit point so it floats slightly above the eyeball, though I'm considering just skipping it for simplicity.

For the nose, I'm finding the surface point nearest the snout tip and attaching a small black sphere there with partial embedding. For the ears, I'm locating surface points near the top-side of the head and planning to use flattened spheres oriented along the normal direction.

Now I'm working out the leg structure: defining a hips joint and spine chain, then setting up front leg roots and IK targets with limb segment lengths and bend directions to get natural knee bending.

I'm figuring out joint naming conventions and chain roles for the legs, using distinct identifiers like "hipFL" for each joint, then setting up the paw geometry as a flattened sphere attached to the ankle bone.

For scattering the back spines along the body surface, I'm filtering out positions near the head and setting a color gradient between cream and brown based on position along each spike.

I'm thinking about adding a small decorative touch — maybe a single fallen maple leaf resting on the spines for an autumn feel — placing it on the body surface near the back, offset upward slightly so it looks naturally perched among the quills, and scaling it down to fit proportionally with the hedgehog's size.

I also need to double-check that point and frame types convert properly for positioning the leaf and eyes, make sure the mirrored ear placement uses the correct side convention, and estimate the triangle count contribution from all the spine sweeps to keep the mesh complexity reasonable.

Now I'm setting up the module scaffolding: importing the builder utilities and types, defining the metadata export for the hedgehog model, and starting to declare the color constants for brown, cream, and other palette values.

I'm structuring the skeleton hierarchy starting with hips, then building a curved spine chain using catmull-rom interpolation across a few points, and beginning to attach the head joint as a child of the spine.

Now I'm defining the body loft from spine stations, the head tube sweep tapering outward from the head joint, and scattering spike hits across the body surface using a filtered random distribution with color varying by position along each spike.

I'm building out the leaf, mirrored leg chains with hip/knee/ankle joints and bend directions for front and hind legs, paw spheres bound to the ankle joints, eyes with glint highlights, nose, and flattened ear discs all placed using nearest-surface hits on the body and head surfaces. I'm finalizing the leaf outline points and returning the root of the model.
